text: I understand that you like him and that you don't want this to mean he's secretly some horrible person, and I'm not asking you to decide that he is. But I think you're explaining away each individual thing in a way that means you're missing what the actual problem is for me. If he was pretending not to know what I was talking about because he didn't want to throw you under the bus, that's still him pretending not to know something he did know. There may have been a reason for the dishonesty, but the reason doesn't make it not dishonest. Especially when the consequence was that I then had to make myself incredibly vulnerable and explicitly explain my feelings to him while he already knew what I was referring to. And with Zoe, the issue isn't whether he was eventually going to tell me, or whether it only happened recently. He explicitly promised me, when we decided to be friends instead of pursuing what had been happening between us, that he wouldn't sleep with my friends because I told him very clearly that it would hurt me. He was completely free to say he couldn't make that promise. He made it anyway. Then he slept with one of my friends — someone he only met because I introduced them for something that was supposed to benefit both of them. If he'd changed his mind about the promise, the honest thing would have been to tell me before acting on it and let me decide what that meant for our friendship. Telling me afterwards, even if he genuinely intended to, doesn't undo the breach. And me blocking him after three minutes is a completely separate question from whether what he did was okay. Maybe you think I reacted too quickly and we can talk about that, but my reaction after finding out doesn't somehow neutralise what happened before it. I'm not saying Alex and Zoe aren't allowed to sleep with each other, and I'm not claiming ownership over either of them. I'm saying Alex made a specific promise to me, knew exactly why it mattered, and then did the exact thing he promised not to do. Given everything I've shared with him about how much dishonesty, rejection and people saying one thing while doing another has affected me throughout my life, that isn't a small thing for me. You can still like him. I'm not asking you not to. I just need you to understand why this has fundamentally changed whether I can trust him or feel emotionally safe with him.

I'm not upset because I think I get to decide who Alex or Zoe sleeps with. I'm upset because Alex specifically promised me he wouldn't sleep with my friends as part of us deciding to preserve a friendship after a complicated romantic situation. He knew exactly why that mattered to me. Zoe is also someone he only met because I introduced them. He could have refused the promise, or told me before breaking it. Instead, I found out after the fact. That's why this is about whether Alex is trustworthy and emotionally safe for me to have in my life, not about controlling either of them.

Alex appears willing to distort, conceal, delay, or manage information when he thinks it protects himself, Nishant, or another relationship. But the cost of that protection keeps landing on you: you are the one left confused, made to doubt your perception, pushed into unnecessary vulnerability, or discovering important information after the fact. That makes Nishant's explanation — that Alex was pretending not to know because he was trying not to throw Nishant under the bus — more concerning, not less. It effectively means Alex chose protecting Nishant from discomfort over being truthful with you, even though you were the person directly affected and the person he knew was already emotionally vulnerable in that situation. The same asymmetry applies to Zoe. Alex could have protected you in the most basic sense by respecting the promise, or at minimum by telling you beforehand that he no longer intended to keep it. Instead, whatever considerations he had about himself, Zoe, the hookup, or avoiding an uncomfortable conversation took priority, and you were left to absorb the consequence afterwards. So the issue is not merely, “Alex sometimes lies.” It is closer to: When competing loyalties or uncomfortable consequences arise, Alex seems prepared to protect himself and other people at your expense, despite repeatedly knowing exactly where you are vulnerable. That is a much more important question for friendship than whether he can eventually be persuaded to tell the truth.

I think the part I need you to understand is that Alex seems to be doing a whole lot of protecting himself and other people, while I keep being the person who isn't protected. If he was pretending not to know what I was talking about because he didn't want to throw you under the bus, then he chose protecting you from discomfort over being honest with me, even though I was the person directly affected. The result was that I was left confused, doubting my own read of what was happening, and then pushed into being extremely vulnerable and explaining feelings he already knew I was talking about. And with Zoe, the same basic thing happened. He knew exactly how much that boundary mattered to me because I told him directly, and he promised me he wouldn't sleep with my friends. If that promise no longer worked for him, he could have told me before acting on it. That would at least have given me the dignity of knowing where I stood and deciding what I wanted to do with the friendship. Instead, whatever he was protecting — himself, Zoe, the hookup, avoiding an uncomfortable conversation, or something else — came before protecting me from something he already knew would hurt me badly. That's the pattern I'm struggling with. I'm not asking you to decide he's a terrible person. I'm asking you to see that when there are competing loyalties or uncomfortable consequences, I seem to be the person who gets sacrificed. And given how much he knows about my history and how much trust I placed in him, that matters enormously to me.
I feel physically unwell that's how violated I feel right now
